requirement.text: At least 75% of the time, the system shall accurately identify a voice sequence argument spoken in English by Handsfree Wearable device users with a natural language of General American English or Standard Canadian English without a dialect or accent.   Assumptions: The device is worn in the recommended device location while standing still. The device user is not wearing facial PPE or a gown. Background noise does not exceed 45 dB. Normal voice conversation level of 60 dB or louder. The argument is up to five syllables (e.g., med-ium, Doc-tor- Jen-nie Smith)   Rationale: To support reliable accuracy for the supported language(s).   Context: Accuracy is the true prediction of the voice sequence argument. Returning multiple matching resources for a correctly identified argument is considered a success.   Sound Level Research: WHO (World Health Organization) recommends that hospital noise limits be 35 dB(A) during the daytime and 30 dB(A) during the nighttime (Hill & LaVela, 2015). EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) and WHO identified perceived speech interference and annoyance levels at 55dB(A) outdoors and 45 dB(A) indoors (CDC). AAMC summarizes many study results of measured hospital noises (Jawadi and Chern): Johns Hopkins Hospital's daily average sound level of 50-60 dB(A). "A 2021 systematic review of 33 studies examining environmental noise in hospitals worldwide found indoor noise levels ranging from 37-88.6 dB(A) during the day and 38.7-68.8 dB(A) in the evening." "Operating rooms (ORs) often surpass 60 dB(A), with peak noise in maxillofacial ORs exceeding 115 dB(A)." A study of Emergency Department (ED) sound levels reports weighted average sound levels of 43 dB and 52.9 dB over 12 hours, with peak levels of 94 dB to 117 dB (Tijunelis et al.). Another study of Emergency Department (ED) sound levels reports noise levels greater than 45 dB 76-96% of the time. The study also cites WHO as recommending that complex communications be spoken at least 15 dB higher than the background noise to be intelligible (Emar et al.).   Sound Level Research Resources: CDC. “Understanding Noise Exposure Limits: Occupational vs. General Environmental Noise | | Blogs | CDC.” Cdc.gov, CDC.gov, 8 Feb. 2016, blogs.cdc.gov/niosh-science-blog/2016/02/08/noise/. Emar, Murad, et al. “Background Noise in an Emergency Department: An Observational Study from Staff and Patient Perspectives.” MedRxiv, 21 May 2022, www.medrxiv.org/content/10.1101/2022.05.20.22275148v1.full. Hill, J. N., & LaVela, S. L. (2015). Noise Levels in Patient Rooms and at Nursing Stations at Three VA Medical Centers. HERD: Health Environments Research & Design Journal, 9(1), 54–63. https://doi.org/10.1177/1937586715592635 Jawadi, Zina, and Alexander Chern. “Hospitals Are Noisy. They Don’t Have to Be.” Association of American Medical Colleges, 10 Aug. 2023, www.aamc.org/news/hospitals-are-noisy-they-don-t-have-be. Tijunelis, Marius A., et al. “Noise in the ED.” The American Journal of Emergency Medicine, vol. 23, no. 3, May 2005, pp. 332–335, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ajem.2005.02.037.

test_cases.description: HFW system should accurately detect voice commands of general english with arguments.
test_cases.setup: Prerequisite: Create an entity hierarchy in ECP and create Shared Services credentials and associate to the facility.  Make sure Allow Voice Login is  enabled  for the facility in configuration.  Make sure  correct  Save Scotty Configuration inputs are saved for the above facility with all  required  settings. Create scotty devices  SD1  in the above facility. Create a practitioner  P1  with official name. Connect the scotty devices  SD1  to Scotty Gateway. Make sure practitioner  P1  is already logged into device  SD1  if necessary (refer to test data set).     Test Data Set(s): HFW Voice Commands - General English - With Arguments  as  [C]

test_cases.description: NEG - Verify that the Language Analysis component does not identify Patient Safety Risk Disable intent for invalid risk indicators.
test_cases.setup: Pre-Requisites: Make sure to have access to Language Analysis component. Test setup depends on the Language Analysis component being used. Refer Module  HFW Language Analysis Component Setup   LLM Context : call-state : Not on a call. alert-state : No active alert to respond to. has-notifications : false   Test Data Sets: HFW Invalid Patient Safety Risk Indicators  as  [R] HFW Enable Patient Safety Risk Commands For Invalid Risk Indicators  as  [C]
test_cases.steps:
Step 1. Send  [C].[Command Phrase]   from first row in  [C]  with  [Risk Indicator]  argument replaced by first row in  [R].[Risk Indicator], [Location]  argument replaced by first row in  [L].[Bed]  and [Non Command Word] argument replaced by first row in  [Non Command Words]  table in  [C].
Step 2. Repeat step #1 for all remaining rows in  [C],  with combinations for all remaining rows in  [R],  but use next unique location (Unit, Room, Bed) in  [L]  for  [Location]  argument and use next non-command word for  [Non Command Word]  argument.
Step 3. Calculate the passing percentage of the voice command intent detection with invalid risk indicator and with location arguments for all rows combined for steps #1 to #2.
test_cases.expectedResults:
Step 1. anguage Analysis component shall not identify the Patient Safety Risk Intent and Language Analysis Response shall contain identified intent as per  [C].[Expected Intent]  for clarification.
Step 2. N/A
Step 3. Voice accuracy shall be at least 75% for voice command intent and argument detection combined.

test_cases.description: POS - Verify the language analysis component accurately identifies the respond to alert intent when user has an active alert without extension.

test_cases.steps:
Step 1. Send  [C].[Command Phrase]   from the first row in  [C]  to Language Analysis component with chat context as having an active alert without extension.
Step 2. Repeat step #1 for all remaining rows in  [C].
